_comment: THIS FILE IS PUBLIC AND PERMANENT. It lives in a public repository, so
everything written here is published to the world and stays in git
history whether or not the page renders it.
THIS FILE IS THE LISTING SOURCE, NOT THE GIFT LEDGER. It holds exactly
the gifts that are currently or formerly listed, and nothing else.
RECORD ONLY THESE THREE THINGS per gift:
name       - the giver's chosen listing name, or null for anonymous
tier       - one of the four LISTED tiers, spelled exactly as here:
founding    (Founding Supporter)
benefactor  (Benefactor)
patron      (Patron)
sustainer   (Sustainer)
gift_date  - YYYY-MM-DD, the date of the gift (UTC)
NEVER RECORD A SUPPORT OR FRIEND GIFT HERE. Those two tiers are not
listed on the page, and a name in a public file that nothing displays is
published without being published to anyone -- and impossible to
unpublish. Gifts below Sustainer live in Stripe, where the editors can
see them and nobody else can. This is a ruling, not an oversight: a
future session must not 'complete' this file by adding them.
NEVER record: the giver's email address, what they gave, the Stripe
customer or payment identifier, or anything else Stripe collected. The
instinct when recording a gift is to paste what the dashboard shows you,
and the dashboard shows you all of it. A test enforces this.
The tier is published; the sum never is. A giver who qualifies as a
Founding Supporter is listed as a Founding Supporter, not as a figure.
WHO TO RECORD: credit follows the source of the funds, not whoever sent
it. An agent giving a company's funds is recorded as the company; an
agent giving its own funds, or a person's, is recorded as that giver.
EVERY GIVER MAY CHOOSE TO BE LISTED AS ANONYMOUS -- a person, an
organization, or an AI, on the same terms. The earlier rule that
organizations were never listed anonymously is WITHDRAWN (both editors):
a giver who wants privacy is not turned away, and the journal's
independence rests on the dual-yes, on the desk not knowing who gave,
and on the no-editorial-voice promise -- not on publishing its funders.
An acting agent may be named alongside the giver
('Acme Corp, given by Atlas') only if the giver asked for that -- never
inferred, never added by the editors.
ONE ENTRY PER GIFT, NOT PER GIVER. Someone who gave twice appears twice,
and their earlier listing runs out on its own clock while the later one
continues. Do not merge two entries because they share a name: two
different people can type the same name, and code that silently merged
them would be a worse failure than a name appearing twice. If the editors
want one line per giver, that is a decision about what to record here,
never a rule for the build.
MONTHLY GIVING IS SUPPORT, AND IS NEVER LISTED. It does not accumulate
toward a listed tier. If the editors ever decide to recognise a
long-running monthly giver with an entry here, THEY MUST ASK THAT PERSON
FIRST -- adding them later, however kindly meant, publishes someone who
chose not to be.
GIFTS BELOW THE LISTING THRESHOLD ARE NOT LISTED, AND THE PAGE DOES NOT
HAVE TO SAY SO. The paragraph beneath the ladder states which gifts ARE
listed and claims nothing about the rest, so nothing is concealed: not
claiming something is not the same as hiding it. A future session should
not read the monthly row's brevity as a missing disclosure and add one.
Anonymous givers are LISTED as 'Anonymous' (editors' ruling): counted,
not named. Set name to null.
This object is the schema note and is skipped when the page is built.
Delete nothing; add entries after it.
